question: What typical Chevron Alignment sign spacing does Table 2C-5 recommend for an advisory speed of 35 to 45 mph and a curve radius of 401 to 700 feet?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a curve with an advisory speed of 35 to 45 mph and a curve radius of 401 to 700 feet, Table 2C-5 shows a typical Chevron Alignment sign spacing of 120 feet. This spacing is a Guidance (recommended) value, measured along the turn or curve from the point of curvature (PC). Standards (mandatory): - "If used, Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed on the outside of a turn or curve, in line with and at approximately a right angle to approaching traffic. Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed at a minimum height of 4 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way." Guidance (recommended): - "The approximate spacing of Chevron Alignment signs on the turn or curve measured from the point of curvature (PC) should be as shown in Table 2C-5." - Per Table 2C-5, an advisory speed of 35 to 45 mph corresponds to a curve radius of 401 to 700 feet and a sign spacing of 120 feet. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 2C-5 shows the row "35 to 45 mph | 401 to 700 feet | 120 feet," and includes the note that the relationship between curve radius and advisory speed shown in the table should not be used to determine the advisory speed. - [Image 2] Page 199 shows Section 2C.08 in context, including the Guidance paragraph directing users to Table 2C-5 and the table itself with the 120-foot spacing for the 35–45 mph / 401–700 feet row. - [Image 3] Page 197 shows Figure 2C-2 (Sheet 1 of 2), illustrating W1-8 chevron placement along a curve with a note to "See Table 2C-5 for spacing of W1-8 signs." Citations: - Table 2C-5 (p.158) - Section 2C.08 Guidance §5 (p.158) - Section 2C.08 Standard §4 (p.158) - Page 199 - Page 197
